title: Fenwick / BIT advanced: 2D, order-statistics, inversions, range-update
relevance: High — inversion counting, “how many ≤ x”, and k-th in a dynamic multiset show up constantly in OAs; range-add / 2D rectangle sum are the CF Div2 C–D upgrade past plain prefix sums.
company_notes: Count smaller elements to the right → LC 315 / Tessoku inversions (Amazon/Meta-style Hard). Order-statistic API: add, delete k-th, or count in [L,R] under updates → Multiset / Salary Queries / List Removals. NumMatrix: update cell, query subrectangle sum → 2D BIT (CSES Forest Queries II; interview API often mirrors LC 308). Many range increments then read the array / range sums → Greg and Array / CSES Range Update / two-BIT RURQ (difference-array interviews that scale to n,q∼10^5).

must_hit.evidence_hint: Names smaller-to-the-right / inversions and reaches for compress + Fenwick frequency scan.

must_hit.point: “Support add value, delete k-th, or count elements in [L,R] under updates” → order-statistic / frequency BIT (Multiset / Salary Queries / List Removals).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps dynamic k-th / range-count-under-updates to a frequency Fenwick API.

must_hit.point: “Many range increments, then read the array / range sums” → BIT-as-difference or two-BIT RURQ; “NumMatrix: update cell, query subrectangle” → 2D BIT.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits range-add family from 2D cell-update + rectangle-sum and names the matching BIT shapes.

must_hit.point: Signal words: count pairs with order constraint, k-th remaining element, many range increments, trees in a subrectangle with toggles, nested segments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signal phrases and ties them to advanced Fenwick patterns rather than plain prefix sums.

hints.2: Smaller-to-the-right → inversion BIT; add/delete k-th / count [L,R] → freq BIT; range increments → diff / two BITs; cell update + subrectangle → 2D BIT.
hints.3: Say: LC 315-style smaller-right → compress+scan freq BIT; Multiset/Salary/List Removals → order-statistic BIT; many range increments → BIT-as-diff or two-BIT RURQ; NumMatrix/LC 308 → 2D BIT; signal words include order pairs, k-th remaining, range increments, subrectangle toggles, nested segments.

phases.goal: State the Fenwick plan for inversions, find_kth, range updates, two-BIT RURQ, 2D rectangles, or BIT-for-DP before coding.

must_hit.point: Inversions / smaller-to-the-right: compress values, scan L→R or R→L, query prefix then add(rank,1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States compress, directional scan, query-then-update on ranks.

must_hit.point: Order statistics: BIT as frequency table; find k-th by binary lifting on prefix sums (find_kth).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes counts in the BIT and binary lifting to the k-th rank.

must_hit.point: Range update: store a difference array in the BIT — add(l,+v), add(r+1,−v), point value = prefix; for range-add + range-sum use two BITs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates one-BIT point query after range add from two-BIT RURQ.

must_hit.point: 2D: nest the i+=i&-i loops; rectangle = inclusion–exclusion of four corners. BIT-for-DP: when transition is max/sum over ranks < v, replace the loop with a Fenwick.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions nested Fenwick loops with four-corner rect and Fenwick replacing a ranks-<v DP loop.

probes: Walk through inversions vs find_kth vs range-add — what does each query and update do on the BIT?

hints.1: Split frequency/order-stat uses from difference/RURQ and from 2D nesting.
hints.2: Inversions: compress, scan, query then add(rank,1); k-th via binary lifting on counts; range add → diff BIT; RURQ → two BITs; 2D → nested loops + four corners.
hints.3: Say: compress+scan query-then-add for inversions; freq BIT + find_kth binary lifting; add(l,+v)/add(r+1,−v) for point query; two BITs for range-add+range-sum; nest i+=i&-i and four-corner inclusion–exclusion; DP max/sum over ranks < v → Fenwick.

phases.goal: Code 1-indexed Fenwick primitives, compression, find_kth walk, difference/two-BIT formulas, and 2D rectangle identity.

must_hit.point: 1-indexed BIT: add(i,δ) via i += i&-i; sum(i) via i -= i&-i; range = sum(r)-sum(l-1); always long long on CF.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes those exact add/sum loops, the two-prefix range, and long long on CF.

must_hit.point: Coordinate compression before any value-as-index BIT when a_i≤10^9; offline-collect all values (array + query endpoints).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Collects all values offline and maps to ranks before indexing the BIT.

must_hit.point: Order statistic find_kth: walk bits of pos while bit[pos+bit] < k (List Removals / Multiset). Range update + range query: two BITs B1,B2 with prefix(i)=i·sum(B1,i)-sum(B2,i) (SPREAD / cp-algorithms).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the binary-lifting k-th walk and the two-BIT prefix formula.
Writes nested Fenwick updates/queries and that exact four-corner identity.

hints.2: i += i&-i / i -= i&-i; compress a_i≤10^9 offline; walk bits while bit[pos+bit] < k; two BITs prefix(i)=i·sum(B1,i)-sum(B2,i); four-corner rect.
hints.3: Spell: 1-indexed add/sum with i&-i and long long; offline compress when a_i≤10^9; find_kth walks bits while bit[pos+bit] < k; RURQ prefix(i)=i·sum(B1,i)-sum(B2,i); rect = S(x2,y2)-S(x1-1,y2)-S(x2,y1-1)+S(x1-1,y1-1).

phases.goal: Catch 1-indexing, compression, overflow, difference off-by-ones, and 2D inclusion–exclusion sign errors.

must_hit.point: Fenwick must stay 1-indexed; add uses i += i&-i and sum uses i -= i&-i — 0-based loops are a default WA.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on 1-indexing and the correct ± i&-i directions.

must_hit.point: Values with a_i≤10^9 need coordinate compression before a value-as-index BIT; collect array values and query endpoints offline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compresses huge values (and query endpoints) before indexing the BIT.

must_hit.point: Always long long on CF for Fenwick sums; range-add point query must do both add(l,v) and add(r+1,-v).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names long long on CF and the closing add(r+1,-v) of the difference update.

must_hit.point: 2D rectangle mistakes: wrong four-corner signs — must be S(x2,y2)-S(x1-1,y2)-S(x2,y1-1)+S(x1-1,y1-1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the inclusion–exclusion signs for the four corners.

probes: What indexing and overflow bugs show up first when coding an advanced Fenwick?
What goes wrong if you skip compression, forget add(r+1,-v), or botch 2D four-corner signs?

hints.1: Check 1-indexing, 64-bit sums, compression, difference endpoints, and 2D signs.
hints.2: 1-indexed ±i&-i; long long on CF; compress a_i≤10^9 offline; add(l,v) and add(r+1,-v); four-corner +/− pattern.
hints.3: Say: stay 1-indexed with i+=i&-i / i-=i&-i; always long long on CF; compress when a_i≤10^9 including query endpoints; range add needs add(r+1,-v); rect = S(x2,y2)-S(x1-1,y2)-S(x2,y1-1)+S(x1-1,y1-1).

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Range update + point query stores a difference array in one BIT — add(l,+v), add(r+1,−v), point = prefix. Range-add + range-sum needs two BITs B1,B2 with prefix(i)=i·sum(B1,i)-sum(B2,i) (SPREAD / cp-algorithms).

Static rectangle sums use the four-corner identity on a 2D prefix (Forest Queries / Counting Points). With point toggles or cell updates plus subrectangle sums, nest Fenwick loops in a 2D BIT (Forest Queries II) at O(log^2 n).

tradeoffs.topic: Naive DP loop over ranks vs BIT-for-DP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When the transition is max/sum over ranks < v, replace the loop with a Fenwick (Flowers, Increasing Subsequence II, Bubble Sort Graph) so each transition uses Fenwick prefix aggregates instead of scanning lower ranks.

tradeoffs.topic: Inversion scan direction L→R vs R→L
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both work after compression: scan L→R or R→L, query how many already seen are < (or >) the current rank, then add(rank,1) — choose the direction that matches “smaller to the left” vs “smaller to the right”.

gotchas.trap: Implementing Fenwick 0-indexed or flipping the i&-i update/query directions.
gotchas.correction: Keep a 1-indexed BIT: add via i += i&-i, sum via i -= i&-i; range = sum(r)-sum(l-1).

gotchas.trap: Using raw values as BIT indices when a_i≤10^9.
gotchas.correction: Coordinate-compress first; offline-collect all values from the array and query endpoints, then map to ranks.

gotchas.trap: Range-add implemented as only add(l,v) without closing the difference.
gotchas.correction: Difference in BIT needs add(l,v) and add(r+1,-v); point value is sum(i).

gotchas.trap: Using int for Fenwick aggregates on Codeforces.
gotchas.correction: Always use long long on CF for Fenwick / prefix-style sums.

gotchas.trap: Wrong signs on a 2D rectangle query.
Broken find_kth walk on a frequency BIT.
gotchas.correction: Binary-lift on prefix sums: walk bits of pos while bit[pos+bit] < k (List Removals / Multiset).
